params.body:
A follow-up on #778, which is merged. The notice is right; its weight was not.

Shane, on seeing it: "wel heel erg zwart/vet, ok met huisstijl?" It was not. The block was `font-semibold` on `text-brand-ink`, so bold on near-black, and it shouted louder than the "Plaats bod" button beside it. A notice that outshouts the action it belongs to loses its authority.

`/huisstijl`, the app's own style page, states the pattern in so many words:

> Zachte achtergrond in de statuskleur, rand in dezelfde kleur.

```blade
<div class="rounded-brand border border-brand-amber/25 bg-brand-amber/5 px-4 py-3 text-sm text-brand-amber">
```

That is what the notice wears now: amber, normal weight. The position above the amount field was what solved Frederik's complaint; the weight was mine to add and mine to take back.

The percent icon is gone as well. `fa-percent` appears exactly once in the whole codebase, in my line, while `fa-info-circle` appears eight times: it is not in the icon set this app ships, so it rendered as a gap. The house pattern carries no icon either.

`ABidOnAVatVehicleSaysExclVatTest` gains one test: a notice carries the status colour and no extra weight. It pins the lesson rather than the exact utility string, so a later redesign of the palette does not fail it.

Verified locally: 22 tests, 847 assertions across the bidding test, the rule-catalogue tests and the stylesheet test.
params.title: The VAT notice wears the house pattern for a notice
